local_inverse_reflection.definition: theta is the FULL two-sided semigroup congruence generated by xy= yx for every e in E(S), x,y in E(eSe). Every generator has the same q-image q(e), so theta subset ker q.
local_inverse_reflection.purity_and_lifting: For pi:S->T=S/theta, pi(s) idempotent implies q(s) idempotent, hence s idempotent. Likewise q descends to a pure CS quotient of T. Thus every target corner-idempotent lifts to an actual source corner-idempotent: pick e lifting the target corner unit, then replace a preimage s by ese and use pi-purity.
local_inverse_reflection.locally_inverse_proof: All idempotents in each local monoid of T commute by the generators. T and its local monoids are regular, so T is locally inverse. Its pure CS projection gives the exact weak-E-unitarity criterion. Any map to a locally inverse semigroup kills the generators, so theta is the least such congruence in this supplied-pure-quotient setting.
local_inverse_reflection.normal_model: Invoke the explicitly NAMED Billhardt-Szendrei2003 theorem, as stated in Szendrei2019 Theorem5.5, to embed T in a Pastijn product of a normal band by CS. The change-of-quotient lemma puts it over the actual supplied q:T->C, not merely an unspecified new quotient.
local_inverse_reflection.kernel_conclusion: For the canonical normal-band presentation with ALL M, the map kappa_N has kernel EXACTLY theta: its target is locally inverse and kills theta, while the separating normal-band model of T proves the reverse inclusion. Therefore ker kappa_V subset theta. Original SEP reduces to faithfulness on idempotents within theta classes, not arbitrary q-fibres. No assertion those classes are rectangular/regular beyond delivered proof is made.
